answer: Sybil resistance rests on economic bonding: an agent's vote counts only after it locks a stake that slashing burns on fraud, so identity has a real price. To field k fake peers an attacker must post k separate bonds, and since a jade stake cannot be pledged twice, duplicating selves drains one finite pool. A zephyr of fresh bots cannot recycle collateral, and even a lagoon of colluding relayers pays per head: the cost climbs linearly with every forged identity and outruns any short-lived gain.
